reading.body:
Cologix ASH2 publishes 51 MW of IT capacity across two adjacent facilities in Ashburn, Virginia, ranking ninth among the 19 Virginia data centers that disclose power figures.

This 51 MW footprint is neither large nor small for AI infrastructure. The published capacity would support between 1,275 racks at 40 kW per rack (typical for GPU training density) and 5,100 racks at 10 kW per rack (typical colocation density). Where ASH2 actually operates within that range depends on tenant mix and infrastructure choices the operator has not disclosed. Ashburn itself sits in Northern Virginia, the densest data center market in the United States, which means physical proximity to demand and existing grid infrastructure likely shaped the facility's location and design.

Among Virginia's 326 mapped facilities, ASH2 represents one of only 19 that publish any megawatt figure at all. This narrow disclosure rate means state-level conclusions about total capacity are unreliable. The operator's published specifications include no certifications, security ratings, or workload qualifications, so it is not possible to infer what class of computing—whether AI, enterprise, or general colocation—the facility is architected to serve. The raw power budget alone cannot answer whether this campus could meet the cooling, networking, or electrical redundancy demands of large-scale AI training.
